reviewer: Codex authoring host; reviewed product diff and independent toolkit boundary

acceptance.evidence: The product verify command no longer reads an active-task configuration or review gate. Tests/demo run from an extracted ZIP without external host-tool configuration; its optional Hook shim returns an empty result.

Generic review, state and Hook helpers are in a separate local Git project at commit 68f18848d55ba239f1819d933d1baf682fef9129, excluded from the product archive. Eight independent tests pass, including CLI use with a non-Node Git fixture. Existing trusted Hook definitions remain unchanged.

Repository CI/release/maintenance use only repository-owned commands and GitHub scripts, without importing the local toolkit. Three operational regression tests and actionlint pass. Project-specific artifact history remains versioned as recommended by the Playbook.

findings.detail: A fixed current task and generic review gate were coupled to npm verify. Those gates and generic tests are now external optional host tools; product checks are independently runnable.
The release gate imported generic SDLC policy from product scripts. Its small repository-specific condition now lives in .github and is tested there.

Junction aliases initially prevented the new external CLI from recognizing its main entry. Module identity now compares real paths while Codex project/trust paths remain unchanged; the actual alias invocation was verified.
Project-specific intent, plan and review records remain alongside code for traceability. The local toolkit is a separate Git workspace, not a second published product.
Review is host self-review, and automatic desktop Hook lifecycle events remain unverified. Remote release verification is provided by the subsequent Actions run.
